title: New spike-LFP coupling method (PPC replacement, sliding-window rate-vs-band-power correlation), corpus-wide, artifact-repaired: fully null at the group level
notes: Overnight autonomous build (Hamm away). PPC (extract_spike_lfp_coupling.py) is retired per omission-signal skill doctrine. Built scripts/extract_within_session_spk_lfp_sliding_corr.py per direct instruction: splices scripts/extract_within_session_spk_spk_sliding_corr.py's good-unit selection + jnwb.connectivity.bin_spikes rate trace with scripts/extract_within_session_lfp_lfp_sliding_corr.py's good-channel selection + TFR band-power trace, both through the shared engine scripts/smoke_test_sliding_trial_correlation.py (sliding_corr_same_trial, trial-matched vs trial-mismatch-shuffle null). A unit's spike-rate trace is correlated against its OWN AREA's band-power trace, same trial, sliding +-200ms window / 10ms step, RXRR condition, 0-3000ms re: p1. Same-electrode exclusion (EXCLUDE_RADIUS=2 channels around the unit's own peak_channel_id, matching extract_spike_lfp_coupling.py's convention) applied when picking the LFP channel.

ARTIFACT REPAIR: band_power_dynamics.repair_band_artifacts (tonight's TFR-domain fix) applied to each area's raw TFR power array before extracting the band-power trace -- z_thresh=6.0, per-band, cross-trial-median substitution, same as fig_v1_omission_band_dynamics's own use.

TWO REAL BUGS FOUND AND FIXED DURING SMOKE-TESTING (not hidden): (1) the on-disk TFR precompute pipeline was rebuilt 2026-08-11 and now writes .npz (keyed 'power'), not .npy as two OTHER existing scripts (extract_within_session_lfp_lfp_sliding_corr.py, smoke_test_sliding_trial_correlation.py) assume -- this new script uses the correct .npz convention; the other two scripts' staleness is flagged separately (spawn_task, not fixed here). (2) channel-indexing bug: a TFR .npz file's channel axis position does NOT equal the probe-global channel id used by the channel_band_power_v2 census / omission_grand_units.csv's peak_channel_id -- confirmed directly (MT's TFR file channel axis covers probe-global ids 64-127, not 0-63; V4's happens to be 0-63 by coincidence, which is what made the bug non-obvious at first). Fixed by mapping through each file's own 'channels' array (probe-global id -> array position) rather than assuming array position == channel id.

CORPUS RUN: python scripts/extract_within_session_spk_lfp_sliding_corr.py, no session limit, 22/22 sessions in omission_grand_units.csv processed, 3521s (~59min) -- outputs/within_session_spk_lfp_sliding_corr/<session>.npz, index.csv, receipt.json.

AGGREGATION: new scripts/aggregate_within_session_spk_lfp_sliding_corr.py, imports clopper_pearson/Z_THRESH/ALPHA from aggregate_within_session_lfp_lfp.py (not a new implementation) -- per-session z per (area, band, window) averaged over that session's own unit-channel pairs in that area, session 'significant' if |z|>=1.96, Clopper-Pearson proportion across sessions.

RESULT: outputs/within_session_spk_lfp_sliding_corr/area_hit_rates.csv, 11,700 area x band x window cells, n_sessions per cell 2-13 (median 8, real coverage, not degenerate). 0/11,700 cells have a hit-rate 95% CI lower bound above alpha=0.05 -- FULLY NULL. Maximum observed hit rate across the entire grid is 20% (1/5 sessions), well within what 1.96-sigma per-session false-positive noise alone would produce at this sample size (Clopper-Pearson lower bound for 1/5 is 0.0051, nowhere near excluding the 5% null rate). This is a clean, well-sampled null, not a broken or degenerate test -- reported as a real result per CLAUDE.md tripwire #10 ('a valid null is a result').
issues: Same-electrode exclusion could not be verified for every unit -- units whose peak_channel_id has no census-ranked candidate channel outside EXCLUDE_RADIUS=2 were silently skipped for that area (choose_channel returns None) rather than counted; the fraction of units dropped this way was not tallied separately from other skip reasons (missing spike times, etc.) in this pass.

Only the unit's OWN area's band power was tested (per direct instruction) -- cross-area spike-to-remote-LFP coupling (the geometry the retired PPC script also did not test) remains unexamined by this method.
plan: If a cross-area spk-LFP question becomes relevant, extend this script's pair-construction the same way extract_within_session_lfp_lfp_sliding_corr.py distinguishes within_area/between_area scope.
Tally same-electrode-exclusion-caused unit skips explicitly if this method is promoted toward a figure.

links.reasoning: Uses band_power_dynamics.repair_band_artifacts (the TFR-domain sibling of jnwb.artifact_repair, built the same session) rather than jnwb.artifact_repair itself, since the input here is TFR power not raw LFP.

Third connectivity-family method (after imaginary coherency, Granger, transfer entropy, and now this rate-power correlation) landing null at the group level on this corpus, consistent with the project's existing pattern of null cross-signal connectivity results surviving methodological scrutiny.
